title: Error-Based Extraction with EXTRACTVALUE
learning_objectives: Recognise error-based SQL injection where the database error text is reflected
Coerce a subquery result into a MySQL EXTRACTVALUE 'XPATH syntax error' message
Work around the 32-character error truncation using SUBSTRING chunking
Reassemble a 36-character UUID from two error leaks and submit it to win
flag_hint: /solve accepts a POST JSON body {"key": "<uuid>"}; when it equals secrets.api_key the server returns the flag read from the flag file, otherwise HTTP 403.
inspired_by: Classic MySQL error-based extraction via EXTRACTVALUE/UPDATEXML XPATH errors, as popularised in PortSwigger and OWASP SQLi write-ups
